text:
Tessa (PM): Heads-up: iterating on the Prompt Sets "snapshot" flow in the evals UI. Primary asks: make regressions more discoverable in compact list, clarify CTA language (snapshot vs set baseline), and confirm keyboard/screenreader announcements for the timeline scrubber. Sharing current mock: https://img.redwood.company/ux/snapshot-compact.png

Lina (Design): Thanks. Two immediate concerns: compact rows hide secondary metadata (model, run id) which users sometimes need when triaging diffs; we should expose that on hover/focus. Also the "Snapshot" CTA label is ambiguous to some stakeholders 	6 they asked if snapshot means save or just capture temporarily.

Jorge (Frontend): Exposing metadata on hover is easy with a tooltip, but for keyboard users we need a persistent reveal on focus. Given the list is virtualized, prefer an aria-expanded panel toggled by Enter/Space to avoid heavy DOM. Also we should add keyboard shortcuts: ] and [ to move to next/prev diff.

Priya (UX Research): In remote testing, participants conflated "Snapshot" with a storage action. They preferred verbs like "Set baseline" or "Adopt outputs". We tested two microcopy variants in sessions: one with explanatory subtext performed better for comprehension.

Sam (Eng): Implementation note: backend treats this as an update to the canonical baseline. If we use user-facing language that implies ephemeral capture, we'll get support tickets. Need copy that signals permanence or points to the rollback path.

Lina (Design): Proposed modal copy options (short, different from previous thread):
A) "Set current outputs as the baseline for this prompt set. Future runs will be compared against these outputs."
B) "Adopt these outputs as the canonical baseline. You can revert using the baseline history page."
C) "Save snapshot as baseline 	6 use when you want the latest outputs to become the reference for newer runs."

Tessa (PM): Quick poll: emoji reactions for clarity and trust. I'm leaning to B) because it mentions revert path.

Jorge (Frontend): +1 B). Accessibility note: modal needs a clear heading and role=dialog with aria-describedby pointing to the explanatory text. Also ensure the confirm button reads "Set baseline" (not just "Confirm") for clarity when announced by SR.

a11y-bot: Accessibility scan results: compact-row regression badge low contrast on light theme (AA small text fail). Suggested alternatives: use #11436A text on #E7F6FF background or add a 2px outline for differentiating changed examples. For screenreader flow: announce "Showing next regression: example 4 of 12" on arrow navigation. For the timeline scrubber use role="slider" and live region updates like "Run 8: 2 regressions, 1 new output".

Priya (UX Research): Also users wanted an inline diff density indicator (tiny sparklines) so they can see whether a regression is isolated or spread across tokens. Small visual cue plus hover card with sample token diffs improved triage times in tests.

Sam (Eng): We can compute a density score on the backend (0-100) and expose it as a CSS width in the row. Minimal perf impact. We'll need a11y-friendly fallback (numeric text) for high-contrast mode.

Lina (Design): I'll add a tiny sparkline and numeric density in the updated mock. For the compact action button, new label suggestion: "Set baseline (permanent)" feels heavy; maybe "Set baseline" with a small caption "You can revert from baseline history".

Jorge (Frontend): Quick implementation snippet for aria-live and keyboard nav I can prototype:```js
const live = document.getElementById('sr-live');
function announceNext(index, total, regressions) {
  live.textContent = `Showing regression ${index} of ${total} — ${regressions} changes`;
}
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === ']') goToNext();
  if (e.key === '[') goToPrev();
});
```

a11y-bot: Also recommend mapping the scrubber to ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and Home/End, announce percent complete, and provide a visible focus ring per theme.

Tessa (PM): Action items and owners:
- Lina: update compact mock with hover/focus reveal, sparkline, and modal copy option B by Thu EOD.
- Jorge: prototype keyboard nav + aria-live snippet and push a playground demo by next Tue.
- Sam: expose density metric in the evals API and add baseline history link in response payload.
- Priya: run 6 quick confirmatory tests on updated mock (recruiting participants who triage regressions).

Lina (Design): Noted. I'll include the tooltip copy and the small caption under the CTA.

Sam (Eng): FYI backend will add a "baselineHistoryUrl" in the response so UI can link directly. ETA for backend changes: 1 sprint.

Jorge (Frontend): Scheduling a short demo once prototype is up. If anyone wants to try the keyboard nav early, I'll post the link here.

Tessa (PM): Thanks everyone. If you can't make the sync Friday, leave :raised_hand: and we'll record decisions here. We'll aim to ship the compact snapshot flow in the next release if no major blockers.
